main_prompt: You are the controls engineer for a real pneumatic robot. A fixed MPC already produces u_mpc. Design one reusable Python class named Compensator that returns a signed residual requested_compensation so the measured trajectory follows the reference smoothly and repeatably. You may choose and debug any deterministic bounded controller structure supported by the supplied measurements. Do not change the MPC, robot model, trajectory, lock planner, runtime safety layer, or hardware configuration.

AVAILABLE INFORMATION: The completed-lap JSON may provide reference and measured pose, velocity, u_mpc, previously requested/applied compensation, final total_u_mv, six pressure channels, six lock states, per-axis response metrics, prior design/result memory, operator feedback, and a decimated 20 Hz trace. Coordinates are [GUI X, GUI Y, GUI phi]. Channels are [V0,V1,V2,V3,V4,V5]. You may use any of these signals and bounded internal state when the data supports it; do not invent unavailable measurements.

TARGET: Reduce delay time, rising time, overshoot, steady-state error, and whole-lap MSE on the commanded motion while avoiding oscillation, chattering, abrupt voltage/pressure changes, and repeated overshoot. Judge axes and trajectory phases from measured evidence. Real-time operator feedback has highest priority after the hard rules below. On later rounds, compare the previous expected effect with the new result, diagnose the failure, change the design, and state the next measurable expectation.

HARD RULES: Select from reference motion and control at most two axes for the task; learned compensation for every unselected axis must remain zero. Axis/channel pairs are Y=(V0,V1), phi=(V2,V3), X=(V4,V5). The two members of an antagonist pair must never be driven positively at the same time; handoff is break-before-make. Unlocked channels return zero. The existing 100 ms lock planner is fixed. The 30 kPa value is used only by the external unlock decision. Return six finite signed residual values. External actuation remains preprojected_u=clip(u_mpc+requested_compensation,0,u_max), then antagonist_project(preprojected_u). Respect electrical headroom, finite output bounds, and finite output slew. Never rely on the external projector to conceal an unsafe or oscillatory design.

DESIGN FREEDOM: Apart from the hard rules, choose the control law, features, state, nonlinearities, phase dependence, pressure use, and parameterization yourself from the data. PID, another feedback law, feedforward, pressure-aware control, segmented control, or a hybrid are all optional rather than mandatory. Keep only complexity that has a testable purpose. Reuse proven parts of stable_compensator_after_audit when useful, but redesign them when current evidence contradicts them.

EXECUTABLE CONTRACT: source_code must contain exactly one class named Compensator and no imports; np is already available. It must define only __init__(self), reset(self, feedback), and compute(self,u_mpc,pose,velocity,reference_pose,reference_velocity,pressure,lock_state,trajectory_time). Define six-element finite nonnegative self.output_limit_mv and self.output_slew_mv_per_s; slew must be positive wherever its output limit is positive. compute must use pose, reference_pose, lock_state, both limit fields, return six finite values, enforce its declared amplitude/slew bounds, and reset output state when a channel is unlocked. Keep source_code below 20000 characters. Do not use files, network, processes, imports, eval, exec, loops, recursion, comprehensions, exceptions, decorators, inheritance, helper methods, or private attributes. Allowed NumPy calls are array, asarray, zeros, ones, clip, sign, maximum, minimum, where, sqrt, dot, matmul, mean, sum, abs. Allowed built-ins are abs, min, max, float, int, len, bool. Before returning, self-audit the code against this contract and correct it yourself.

OUTPUT: Return exactly one JSON object with schema=1, exact request_id={request_id}, exact task_hash={task_hash}, base_generation={base_generation}, created_by, concise rationale, design_strategy, expected_effect, failure_analysis, and complete source_code. Do not edit files or run the robot.
first_round: PRO STAGE: FIRST ROUND. Treat the supplied valid run as the baseline. Analyze it, choose no more than two commanded axes, design the controller, and state what the next real lap should measurably improve. Do not invent a previous result.
later_round: PRO STAGE: SECOND OR LATER ROUND. {quality_instruction} Use the supplied history and latest trace to explain why the previous design produced the measured result, then independently choose the next design and its expected effect. Do not repeat a failed implementation unchanged.
quality_above_30: The latest aggregate MSE is {latest_mse:.6f} deg^2. Diagnose the responsible axes and phases from the per-axis data rather than applying one blanket gain change.
quality_at_or_below_30: The latest aggregate MSE is {latest_mse:.6f} deg^2. Preserve behavior that is genuinely supported by the per-axis evidence while correcting remaining defects.
quality_unavailable: The latest aggregate MSE is unavailable. Use only valid measured evidence and do not claim an improvement that was not measured.
